A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same KVSmooth paper, including Appendices A–F. All 18 pages were compared using text extraction and rendering. Pages 2–18 are pixel-identical; page 1 differs only in its arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original benchmark evaluations and ablations. Appendices C, D, and F provide efficiency measurements, sensitivity analyses, and qualitative outputs.

after.justification: The original benchmark evaluations, ablations, efficiency measurements, sensitivity analyses, and qualitative outputs remain in Section 5 and Appendices C, D, and F.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E retain identical KV-cache EMA smoothing, entropy-guided coefficient adaptation, clipping, and inference algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same CHAIR/COCO, OPOPE, AMBER, and Object HalBench coverage, including the same object-sampling scenarios and qualitative examples.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain Baseline, PAI, OPERA, VCD, SPARC, and MiddleLayer. The comparator sets in the trade-off plots, Table 3, and efficiency Table 5 also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix B retain the same three 7B models, greedy decoding with a 512-token maximum, metrics, and sampling procedures, including 500 COCO validation images for CHAIR.

E4.justification: The smoothing-location and adaptive-coefficient ablations, precision–recall trade-offs, efficiency comparisons, parameter sensitivity analyses, and Appendix F case studies are identical.

E5.justification: Figure 1 retains the same 200-image analysis and 95% confidence-interval reporting. No repeated-run, seed, significance-testing, or uncertainty-reporting information changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative outputs match. For example, Table 1 retains LLaVA-1.5 baseline/KVSmooth CHAIR_S values of 41.8/18.2 and F1 values of 77.5/79.2 in both versions.

T1.justification: The attention and entropy definitions, Gaussian assumptions, MAP-to-EMA derivation in Section 4.1 and Appendix A, and remaining mathematical expressions are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about entropy-based sink identification and training-free adaptive smoothing that reduces hallucination while preserving object coverage and efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning semantic drift, attention sinks, variance propagation, and precision–recall trade-offs are unchanged. Appendix D retains the same discussion of performance degradation from smoothing very early or final layers.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, benchmark instructions, and pseudocode are identical, including smoothing layers 3–31, queue length 15, and model-specific reference coefficients. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 43 references and identical related-work discussion and positioning relative to decoding, attention-reweighting, and attention-sink methods.

P1.justification: Only the marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 4 February 2026 to v2 dated 11 March 2026. Manuscript wording, title, authors, section order, and appendix structure are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–10, Tables 1–5, Algorithms 1–2, captions, and manuscript layout are unchanged. The version/date stamp update introduces no figure, table, or layout revision.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and presentation remain identical throughout the main paper and appendices. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp does not meaningfully improve or diminish paper quality.
